title: Aim a loaded inspection arm and lock it at the set angle
instruction: Set the inspection arm on the post to 15 degrees above horizontal and lock it there. 1. Take hold of the black inspection head at the end of the arm and support it. 2. Swing the arm up until it points 15 degrees above horizontal (the head's centre 5.2 cm higher than the hinge). 3. Keep the arm at that angle while the other gripper turns the orange knob on top of the post clockwise, seen from above, until it stops; this locks the hinge. If the arm is already locked at another angle, first turn the knob counter-clockwise to free it. 4. Open both grippers and move them away from the arm and the knob. 5. The arm must stay at 15 degrees above horizontal on its own.
context: Setting up an inspection or camera fixture: one hand holds a loaded adjustable arm at the required angle against gravity while the other hand tightens its indexed clamp, and the setting must hold after both hands let go.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the two arm bases, y to the left, from the midpoint between the bases; heights above the table top. A grey post (3 x 4 cm, 14 cm tall) stands on a 10 x 8 x 0.6 cm foot plate clamped to the table, centred at (29.5, 8) cm. A horizontal hinge on the post's -x side, at (25, 8) cm and 12 cm high, pivots about the x axis. From it a 20 cm arm (1.6 x 1.2 cm bar, 60 g) points toward -y and carries a black inspection head (4 x 6 x 3.5 cm block, 250 g, orange lens on its far end) centred 20 cm from the hinge axis. The hinge moves between a lower stop at 26 degrees below horizontal and an upper stop at 45 degrees above. At the start the arm rests on its lower stop. An orange clamp knob (ridged round, 4 cm diameter, 2.5 cm tall, 120 g, die-cast) sits on a stem 1.2 cm above the post top, at (29.5, 8) cm, axis vertical; it starts loose. Turning it clockwise (seen from above) between 150 degrees and its 170-degree stop meshes a 72-tooth serrated lock (5-degree steps) in the hinge at the step nearest to the arm's current angle. The target elevation is +15 degrees: the arm rises from the hinge toward -y, with the head centre 5.2 cm above the hinge axis (17.2 cm above the table). Intended physical reconstruction: a rigid metal post and foot plate, a lightweight hollow metal arm, and a polymer dummy head ballasted to the specified mass; the knob is die-cast metal. These are construction specifications for this original analogue, not measured properties of a commercial fixture.
scoring: Elevation is measured from the arm body's actual pose (degrees above horizontal); lock state from the knob's actual rotation; gripper state from the measured finger opening and the TCP distance to the head and knob centres. 0.25 once the head has been raised within 10 degrees of +15; 0.5 once it has been within 3 degrees; 0.75 while the lock is meshed and the arm is within 3 degrees. 1.0 (success, trial ends) when the lock is meshed, the arm is within 3 degrees of +15, both grippers are at least 80 % open with their TCPs at least 7 cm from the head and knob centres, and this holds for 2 s with the elevation deviating no more than 2 degrees from its value at the start of that released-hold window. Non-finite states score 0. The untouched start scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: the arm returns to its lower stop, the knob to its loose position and the lock disengages.
fidelity: Rigid-body, reduced-order simulation with an ideal frictionless free hinge. Measured knob rotation engages the nearest 5-degree tooth at 150 degrees and releases below 130 degrees. The engaged clamp uses a spring-damper (2 N m/deg, 0.02 N m s/deg), capped at 20 N m. Knob travel is 170 degrees with viscous damping. Parameters are authored for this original fixture analogue; the inspection head is a passive load.
